thread:
ellie: Quick heads-up — planning to enable feature flag `batch_coalesce_prefetch` to 10% canary in prod today at 17:00 PT. Want to capture owners, exact audience, and rollback thresholds here. TL;DR: 10% canary, 15m burn, watch p50/p95, 5xxs.

kai: Can you confirm the canary audience? Is this traffic-sliced by region or customer tier? Also want the expected perf delta baseline.

ellie: Audience is `canary-aud-v2` (non-enterprise, randomized 10%). Region: us-west-2 primary, us-east as fallback. Baseline we expect +~1–3ms p50 on token generation; p95 should be unchanged.

marta: Linking the PR and config: https://git.redwood/internal/PR/4862 — adds the flag wiring + safety guard. Please review the small config guard I added to avoid enabling for enterprise tags.

jamal: I can own live-watch. Suggested automatic rollback triggers I recommend:
- p50 regress >20% vs baseline for 5 minutes
- p95 regress >15% for 5 minutes
- 5xx rate >0.5% sustained for 3 minutes
- error budget alerts firing (SLO page)

Also add this to the incident template so we can open quickly.

sam: Quick ask — can we exclude heavy batch jobs and internal perf tests from the canary? We saw noise last time when a scheduled job hit canary nodes.

ellie: Yes — the audience excludes `internal-scheduler` and `perf-suite` tags. Added note in PR.

jamal: Rollback command for oncall if needed (keeps it quick):
```
# set canary to 0% immediately
/infra/ffctl set batch_coalesce_prefetch --percent=0 --env=prod
# or via ops-api
curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer $OPS' https://ops.redwood/api/flags/batch_coalesce_prefetch -d '{"percent":0}'
```

jamal: I'll be oncall at 17:00 — I'll run the smoke checklist and keep a 15m watch window. If any threshold trips, I hit rollback and open an incident.

ellie: Perf quick numbers (baseline last hour):
- generation tokens p50: 48ms
- p95: 210ms
- 5xx rate: 0.08%
Expected with canary: p50 49–51ms, p95 within ±5%.

kai: Please enable tracing sampling for canary to 50% so we can debug tail issues quickly. Also add a log marker in the runtime so we can filter coalesce paths: `X-FF-BATCHCO` in request logs.

ellie: Done — tracing sampling bumped and log marker added in PR.

marta: I added a small guard in rollout config to stop automatic scale-downs for canary nodes for the first 10 mins (so we don't lose KV cache warmup).

sam: Code review left a small comment about a missing unit test for the gating path; @marta please address if quick, otherwise we can merge with a follow-up but note the risk.

marta: I can add a tiny test in 20m.

deploy-bot: rollout-scheduler: Scheduled `batch_coalesce_prefetch` canary (10%) for 2025-11-02T17:00:00-07:00. Owner: ellie.

ellie: Plan: enable at 17:00 PT, 15m burn, then escalate to 25% for 30m if healthy, otherwise rollback. I'll ping here at start and after the 15m gate. Thanks all — tagging owners: @jamal (oncall), @marta (PR), @kai (tracing + metrics), @sam (exclusions). :thumbsup:

sam: I'll watch cost and batching dashboards during the burn. If anything odd, I'll post graphs here.

jamal: Ready. I'll open a short-lived watch incident channel at 17:00 (incidents/create canary-watch-191345).

ellie: Awesome — closing async checklist. Post any last-minute concerns here and I'll delay if needed.
